chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If a man appoints his brother as executor of his will and he (the brother) is absent, then it is not permissible for him to refuse his appointment as executor, because if he were present and he refused to accept it, someone else would be sought.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: Appointed as executor of a will; designated to carry out testamentary wishes
key_terms.غَائِب: Absent, not physically present at the time of appointment
key_terms.يَرُدَّ: To reject, refuse, decline the appointment

ai.seo_question: Can an absent person refuse to be executor of a will in Islamic law according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that an absent person who has been appointed as executor of a will cannot refuse the appointment. The legal reasoning given is that an absent person has no greater right to refuse than a present one — and even a present person who refuses simply means another executor must be found. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that wills (wasaya) create binding obligations when the testator has no other recourse.
